question: Can a language model learn continually from expert demonstrations without an explicit reward by sampling its own trajectories and distilling a demonstration-conditioned version of itself, while preserving earlier skills and general capabilities?

key_findings.claim: Author method: SDFT uses one model in two contexts, sampling a trajectory from the query-only student and matching the token distribution of an EMA teacher that additionally sees a query-specific expert demonstration.
key_findings.evidence: The formal presentation minimizes reverse KL on student rollouts, and Algorithm 1 evaluates both student and demonstration-conditioned teacher log probabilities on each sampled sequence before updating the student and EMA teacher. In the implemented system the authors choose a full-vocabulary analytic per-token estimator, one rollout per prompt, and full-parameter fine-tuning; this is on-policy with respect to generated outputs, although the prompts and demonstrations remain an offline fixed dataset.

anchors.section: Algorithm 1, student rollout, analytic gradient, and EMA update

key_findings.claim: Author interpretation, conditional rather than general: reverse-KL SDFT is equivalent to maximizing an implicit trust-region reward only if the demonstration-conditioned policy already approximates the unknown optimal next policy.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 3-5 define a reward from the log ratio of the conditioned policy and current policy and recover reverse-KL optimization under the stated in-context assumption. The only direct check uses ToolAlpaca: the Qwen2.5-7B base scores 42%, the conditioned teacher 100%, and manual review covers 50 traces; the teacher is 0.68 nats from the frozen base versus 1.26 for SFT. This supports teacher usefulness on one task but does not verify equality to the trust-region optimum, the unknown reward, or the changing policy at every continual-learning step.

anchors.section: Section 3.1, Equations 3-5 and the in-context assumption

key_findings.claim: Author-reported skill-learning result: SDFT is the only tested adaptation method that nearly preserves the base six-benchmark average while also producing the highest new-task accuracy on all three skill tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Table 5 reports Science Q&A accuracy/prior average of 70.2/64.5 for SDFT, compared with base 32.1/65.5, SFT 66.2/53.4, re-invoke 66.0/60.2, and DFT 54.8/60.2. Tool use is 70.6/65.4 for SDFT versus base 42.9/65.5 and SFT 63.2/56.0; medical is 40.2/65.4 versus base 30.1/65.5 and SFT 35.5/60.2. These are exact table values, but no per-cell uncertainty is tabulated despite the appendix's default three-seed/95% CI statement.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported knowledge-injection result: on nine 2025 Wikipedia disaster articles, SDFT approaches the paper's oracle retrieval condition and substantially exceeds continued pretraining and question-answer SFT, especially out of distribution.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 gives strict/lenient/OOD accuracy of 89/100/98 for SDFT, 80/95/80 for SFT, 9/37/7 for continued pretraining, 0/0/0 for the base, and 91/100/100 for an Oracle RAG system that is always supplied the correct article. The corpus is about 200,000 tokens, GPT-5 generates roughly five times as many QA tokens, and GPT-5-mini judges outputs, so the result demonstrates performance in a synthetic generator/judge pipeline rather than ordinary retrieval or naturally collected knowledge updates.

anchors.section: Appendix B.3, Wikipedia corpus, GPT-5 data generation, and evaluator prompt

key_findings.claim: Author negative and scaling result: self-distillation depends on sufficient in-context capability and can reverse SFT's reasoning degradation, but the advantage is absent at the smallest tested scale.
key_findings.evidence: The scale sweep reports that 3B SDFT underperforms SFT, while the SDFT-SFT gap is about four points at 7B and seven at 14B. On Olmo-3-7B-Think, the base scores 31.2 with 4,612 generated tokens, SFT falls to 23.5 and 3,273 tokens, and SDFT rises to 43.7 with 4,180 tokens. Response length is only a proxy for reasoning depth and SDFT remains shorter than the base, but the accuracy reversal is a substantive negative result for SFT and a positive result for SDFT.

anchors.section: Section 4.5, Figure 5 scale sweep and Table 2 reasoning-model result

key_findings.claim: Reviewer evaluation audit: the sequential three-skill experiment does not by itself establish the abstract's unrestricted 'without performance regression' claim.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 linearly normalizes each task so 0 is the base model and 1 is the maximum attained by either algorithm, rather than reporting absolute accuracies; only one task order is shown, and numeric confidence intervals are absent. The broader Pareto figures and Table 5 are single-task adaptations, not the three-step sequence. Thus the sequence supports better retention than SFT in this order but cannot rule out smaller regressions, order effects, or scale effects hidden by normalization.

anchors.section: Table 5, single-task rather than sequential results

key_findings.claim: Internal objective contradiction: the IRL equivalence is proved for exact sequence-level reverse KL, whereas the practical method switches direction and uses a sequence-level-biased per-token estimator.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 says reverse KL is theoretically appropriate but that the practical implementation uses forward KL for better performance. Appendix A.1, however, derives the adopted full analytic per-token expression as an estimator of student-to-teacher reverse KL and admits that it is sequence-level biased because it omits the effect of an early token on future state distributions; Algorithm 1 cites that appendix expression as the main update. The paper therefore leaves the implemented divergence direction internally ambiguous and does not prove that either the stated forward-KL implementation or the biased reverse-KL proxy maximizes the implicit reward in Equations 3-5.

anchors.section: Section 3, reverse-KL objective and practical forward-KL statement

key_findings.claim: Reviewer confound audit: several headline comparisons combine privileged external model assistance, synthetic selection, and evaluator coupling that are not reflected by the term 'self-distillation.'
key_findings.evidence: Science demonstrations are sampled up to eight times from GPT-4o and one correct response is retained, yielding 100% training coverage. Medical evaluation uses GPT-5-mini. Knowledge questions are generated by GPT-5 from the same articles and judged by GPT-5-mini, and the retrieval baseline is an oracle that always receives the correct article. All methods are swept and the checkpoint with best target validation is reported, while retention is not a selection criterion. These choices can improve label quality and target scores, but they obscure how much gain comes from self-teaching versus privileged data construction and selection.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported ablation and cost boundary: cheaper or more literal variants fail, while the chosen stable implementation costs materially more than SFT.
key_findings.evidence: Offline teacher distillation improves over SFT but underperforms on-policy SDFT; the frozen-base teacher underperforms, the current-student teacher diverges, and EMA is stable. Full text plus answer reaches 89% strict knowledge accuracy versus 75% for text only and 37% for answer only. Rao-Blackwellization has no measurable gain, multiple trajectories give negligible improvement, and one trajectory is retained. SDFT is reported at roughly 2.5× SFT FLOPs and 4× wall-clock time.

Appendix A.1-A.2, estimator, rollout, and context ablations

method.core_idea: Turn every expert demonstration into privileged context for the current model, use that context-conditioned model as a teacher on outputs sampled by the query-only model, and distill the contextual behavior back into parameters so learning occurs under the student's generated-token distribution.
method.mechanism: For each pair (x,c), SDFT samples y from the student on x, scores the same prefixes with an EMA copy conditioned on x and c, and updates the student using a full-vocabulary analytic token-divergence estimator. The EMA tracks improvement while damping self-feedback instability. The paper interprets exact reverse-KL matching as a trust-region/IRL step, but the practical text says forward KL while Appendix A.1/Algorithm 1 specify a biased reverse-KL-style analytic expression; the reported experiments do not resolve which direction the code uses.
assumptions: The base model is capable enough to infer the intended skill or answer from a single query-specific demonstration in context.
The demonstration-conditioned distribution is a useful approximation to a trust-region-optimal next policy, even though that optimum and its reward are not observed.
A demonstration is available for every training query and is expert-quality; non-expert, noisy, or unstructured demonstrations are not tested.
The same tokenizer/model can evaluate teacher and student distributions over student-generated prefixes.
EMA teacher lag stabilizes the coupled teacher-student system without making the teacher too stale.
A biased analytic per-token objective is an adequate practical proxy for the sequence-level reverse-KL objective used in the theory.
Greedy exact-match or LLM-judge accuracy and a six-benchmark arithmetic mean adequately summarize new and prior capabilities.
Results on Qwen2.5-7B/other tested scales and one sequential task order transfer to broader continual-learning settings.

techniques.role: Creates a stronger teacher from the same model by supplying query-specific privileged context.
Samples the states/tokens on which supervision is applied from the current student rather than replaying expert outputs.
Tracks student progress while reducing the divergence observed with an instantaneous self-teacher.
Marginalizes each next-token divergence over the vocabulary for lower-variance updates, at the cost of sequence-level bias.
Relates exact reverse-KL distillation to a log-ratio reward and trust-region policy improvement under a strong in-context assumption.
Measures target-task accuracy jointly with an average over six pre-existing capability benchmarks.
Applies the method to science, tool-use, and medical skills in one order to test cumulative learning.

evaluations.setting: Single-task Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct adaptation on SciKnowEval Chemistry L-3, ToolAlpaca, and English HuatuoGPT-o1, normally over three seeds.
evaluations.metric: New-task accuracy paired with the arithmetic mean of HellaSwag, HumanEval, IFEval, MMLU, TruthfulQA, and Winogrande.
evaluations.result: SDFT reports 70.2/64.5 on science, 70.6/65.4 on tool use, and 40.2/65.4 on medical. Relative to the base, the prior average changes from 65.5 to 64.5 or 65.4 while target accuracy rises from 32.1, 42.9, and 30.1 respectively.
evaluations.baseline: Base, SFT, SFT plus re-invoke, and DFT; Table 5 gives every exact per-benchmark value.

evaluations.setting: Knowledge acquisition from about 200,000 tokens of nine post-cutoff 2025 Wikipedia disaster articles with GPT-5-generated QA and GPT-5-mini judging.
evaluations.metric: Strict, lenient, and out-of-distribution answer accuracy.
evaluations.result: SDFT scores 89/100/98; SFT 80/95/80; continued pretraining 9/37/7; base 0/0/0; Oracle RAG 91/100/100.
evaluations.baseline: Base, continued pretraining, QA SFT, and oracle retrieval supplied the correct source article.

evaluations.setting: Three sequential skill updates in a single science/tool/medical task order.
evaluations.metric: Per-task performance normalized so base equals 0 and the maximum over SFT/SDFT equals 1, plus unrelated prior capabilities.
evaluations.result: Figure 3 shows SDFT accumulating all three skills with much less visible regression than SFT, but provides no absolute table, alternative orders, or numerical interval for the sequential run.
evaluations.baseline: Sequential SFT under the same normalized visualization.

evaluations.setting: Qwen-family scale sweep on science QA and pass@k up to k=128.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy gap between SDFT and SFT and pass@k.
evaluations.result: SDFT is worse than SFT at 3B, about four points better at 7B, and about seven points better at 14B; pass@k improvements persist through 128, arguing against a pure entropy-collapse explanation.
evaluations.baseline: SFT at matched model sizes and sampling budgets.

evaluations.result: Base is 31.2/4,612; SFT is 23.5/3,273; SDFT is 43.7/4,180. The result shows an accuracy and length collapse under SFT, although length does not directly measure reasoning quality.

evaluations.setting: Knowledge-context, KL-estimator, trajectory-count, and teacher-policy ablations.
evaluations.metric: Strict accuracy, training stability, downstream performance, and qualitative measurable gain.
evaluations.result: Full text plus answer gives 89% versus text-only 75% and answer-only 37%; the analytic estimator is most stable despite bias; Rao-Blackwellization and multiple rollouts give no measurable/negligible gain; frozen teacher underperforms and the current-student teacher diverges, while EMA is stable.
evaluations.baseline: Alternative context components, partial/Rao-Blackwellized estimators, multiple rollouts, and frozen/current teachers.

evaluations.setting: On-policy versus offline distillation and compute comparison.
evaluations.metric: Target/retention performance, FLOPs, and wall-clock time.
evaluations.result: Offline distillation from the improved teacher beats SFT but remains below on-policy SDFT. SDFT is reported to use about 2.5× SFT FLOPs and about 4× wall-clock time.
evaluations.baseline: SFT, teacher-output SFT, offline teacher distillation, and SDFT.

limitations: Author-acknowledged: SDFT critically depends on a base model with strong in-context learning; the 3B result is worse than SFT.
Author-acknowledged: the method cannot readily induce a fundamental behavior absent from the base, such as converting a non-reasoning model into an explicit chain-of-thought model.
Author-acknowledged: some forgetting remains, and learning from noisy, non-expert, or unstructured demonstrations is left for future work.
Author-acknowledged: SDFT incurs about 2.5× the FLOPs and 4× the wall-clock time of SFT.

Reviewer-identified: the demonstrated IRL equivalence assumes an unverified trust-region-optimal contextual teacher and applies to exact reverse KL, while the practical text says forward KL and the appendix/algorithm specify a biased reverse-KL-style estimator.
Reviewer-identified: 'self' training still relies on GPT-4o-selected science demonstrations, GPT-5-generated knowledge QA, and GPT-5-mini medical/knowledge judges.
Reviewer-identified: Oracle RAG always sees the correct article, so it is not a realistic retrieval baseline.
Reviewer-identified: target-validation checkpoint selection and method-specific epoch sweeps do not jointly optimize or independently preregister retention.
Reviewer-identified: the three-step continual result uses one task order and a cross-method normalization that hides absolute changes and uncertainty.

Reviewer-identified: only a narrow collection of skill/knowledge datasets and mostly Qwen-family models are studied; long task streams, domain shifts, adversarial demonstrations, safety alignment, and deployment drift are absent.
Reviewer-identified: the six prior benchmarks are averaged without accounting for scale, task importance, or multiple-comparison uncertainty, and most exact confidence intervals are not tabulated.
failure_modes: A weak model fails to turn a demonstration into a better contextual distribution, making self-distillation worse than ordinary SFT at 3B.
Using the instantaneous student as its own teacher amplifies stochastic token-probability changes and can make training diverge.
A frozen teacher is stable but cannot track newly acquired competence and underperforms the EMA teacher.
Text-only context provides a weak supervisory signal; answer-only context is worse still in the knowledge task.
A biased tokenwise KL proxy can optimize local next-token agreement without following the sequence-level reward-improvement gradient claimed by the theory.
Incorrect, noisy, stylistically mismatched, or copied demonstrations may teach the wrong intent or induce memorization; these cases are untested.
Longer continual streams may accumulate EMA lag and residual forgetting even when a three-task sequence looks stable.
External generator/judge coupling may inflate scores on synthetic knowledge questions without improving independently authored questions.
The extra generation and teacher forward pass can make the method impractical when throughput or memory, rather than data quality, is the limiting resource.
reusable_insights: Privileged context can create a teacher without a separate larger model; distilling it on student-generated prefixes is a general way to turn inference-time information into an on-policy learning signal.
Separate where prompts come from from where outputs come from: SDFT is offline over inputs/demonstrations but on-policy over generated trajectories.
EMA is a useful stability device when the same parameterized system supplies both targets and updates.
Measure target plasticity and prior-capability stability jointly; a high target score alone can hide severe forgetting.
Estimator direction and bias must match the theorem: if the proof concerns sequence reverse KL but code uses a tokenwise forward proxy, report the practical objective as a separate algorithm.
In-context competence is a gating variable for self-training; scale sweeps should be treated as a capability threshold, not merely a smooth scaling curve.
Generator/evaluator provenance is part of the treatment: external models used to select demonstrations or judge answers should be ablated and independently audited.
open_questions: Does SDFT retain its advantage over many more tasks, multiple task orders, repeated revisitation, and nonstationary or adversarial demonstration quality?
Which divergence direction does the released implementation actually use, and can that exact analytic update be connected to a valid sequence-level reward or monotonic policy-improvement theorem?
How should a demonstration be selected when several examples express conflicting styles, solutions, or levels of expertise?
Can noisy/unstructured user interactions be converted into safe contextual teachers without amplifying errors?
What part of the science and knowledge gains remains when demonstrations, QA generation, and judging use independent human-authored sources?
Can adaptive rollout counts, low-rank updates, cached teacher logits, or smaller EMA teachers close the 2.5× FLOP/4× wall-clock gap?
At what measurable in-context-learning threshold does SDFT become preferable to SFT, and can that threshold be predicted before training?
How do SDFT and concurrent OPSD/SDPO compare under a shared codebase, data, objective direction, and continual-learning protocol?

competitive_landscape.title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
competitive_landscape.difference: Agarwal et al.'s GKD already trains a student on its own generated sequences while a teacher supplies token feedback, directly supplying SDFT's on-policy distillation mechanism. SDFT's narrower addition is to make the same model a query-specific demonstration-conditioned teacher and study continual acquisition rather than model compression with a separate teacher.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning by Distilling Context
competitive_landscape.difference: Snell et al. already condition a model on instructions or scratchpads and fine-tune that same model to reproduce the gain without context. Their training uses synthetic inputs and context-derived targets rather than correcting current student rollouts; SDFT adds on-policy output sampling and per-query expert demonstrations, not the basic contextual self-teacher idea.

competitive_landscape.title: Self-Distillation Bridges Distribution Gap in Language Model Fine-Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. previously introduced a method also named Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), using model-generated data to stay near the original LLM distribution and preserve instruction following/safety during task fine-tuning. The present SDFT instead distills a demonstration-conditioned teacher on current student trajectories; its name and broad anti-forgetting claim are therefore not novel even if the mechanism differs.

competitive_landscape.title: Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. systematically attribute RL's lower forgetting to on-policy data across Llama/Qwen families and show approximately on-policy data can suffice. SDFT operationalizes that principle when only demonstrations are available, but does not originate the on-policy-retention finding and tests a narrower sequential stream.

competitive_landscape.title: RL's Razor: Why Online Reinforcement Learning Forgets Less
competitive_landscape.difference: Shenfeld et al. argue that on-policy RL selects new-task solutions close to the base policy in KL and validate lower forgetting in language and robotic models. The current paper replaces an explicit reward with privileged demonstration context, but its KL-minimal continual-learning premise and authorship directly continue this antecedent.

competitive_landscape.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhao et al.'s OPSD has the same central construction: one LLM is teacher and student under different contexts, the teacher sees privileged verified traces, and token divergence is minimized on student rollouts. OPSD focuses on mathematical reasoning and token efficiency, whereas the target paper's defensible distinction is continual skill/knowledge retention and EMA implementation; broad priority for on-policy contextual self-distillation is shared.

competitive_landscape.title: Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation
competitive_landscape.difference: Hübotter et al.'s SDPO conditions the current model on rich environment feedback and distills its feedback-aware predictions into the policy, likewise avoiding an external teacher and producing dense token supervision. It addresses RLVR credit assignment with runtime/judge feedback, while SDFT addresses demonstration-only continual learning; both independently occupy the conditioned-self-teacher design space.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a simple new way to perform true on-policy learning directly from demonstrations: use a demonstration-conditioned version of the model as its own teacher, thereby acquiring skills and knowledge continually without an explicit reward and without performance regression.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines student rollouts, a query-specific contextual EMA teacher, and token-distribution matching; it reports strong target/retention trade-offs on three skills, 89/100/98 knowledge accuracy, one three-task sequence, scale/pass@k behavior, reasoning preservation, and teacher/context/estimator ablations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the evaluation and continual-learning packaging of per-instance demonstration-conditioned on-policy self-distillation, not on-policy distillation, context distillation, self-distillation for retention, or the general claim that on-policy data forgets less. OPSD independently matches the core privileged-context/student-rollout construction, and SDPO matches conditioned self-teaching with feedback. The broad IRL/continual-learning claim is further narrowed because the practical text's forward-KL statement conflicts with the biased reverse-KL-style appendix/algorithm and neither is the exact sequence-level algorithm analyzed; the three-task 'no regression' evidence is also normalized and single-order.
